output: {"objective":"Find the molecular mechanism that best explains the loss of function of BTK-p.Arg28His (BTK, UniProt Q06187) and test it with one targeted computational test.","subject":{"gene":"BTK","variant_id":"BTK-p.Arg28His","accession":"Q06187","position":28,"reference_residue":"R","alternate_residue":"H","protein_change":"p.Arg28His"},"events":49,"current_favourite":"H1","hypotheses":[{"id":"H1","mechanism_class":"protein_interaction","starting_rank":1,"statement":"R28H disrupts the IP6-dependent PH-TH dimer interface of BTK. The His side chain at position 28 cannot make the contacts the arginine makes across the dimer, so the dimer does not form and BTK activation at the membrane is impaired.","supports":["E9","E11","E5","E7"],"would_refute":"A model of the PH-TH dimer (built from the IP6-bound PH domain structures, for example by superposing 1B55 on the E41K dimer) shows residue 28 with no atom within about 5 Å of the partner protomer in any predicted dimer pose, and the R28H change does not alter the interface contact count or buried surface area.","latest_verdict":"untested","label":"agent-generated hypothesis"},{"id":"H2","mechanism_class":"ligand_binding","starting_rank":2,"statement":"The R28 side chain is part of the inositol-phosphate headgroup pocket of the BTK PH domain. Replacing arginine with histidine removes the positive charge and the geometry needed to coordinate the phosphate groups of Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 or IP6, which reduces ligand affinity and membrane recruitment.","supports":["E6","E17","E13","E15"],"would_refute":"In ligand-bound PH-domain structures (1B55 with IP4, and any other inositol-phosphate-bound entry), residue 28 has no atom within about 4 Å of any ligand phosphate oxygen, and an R28H model docked or superposed with IP4 shows the same ligand contacts and binding energy as the wild type within the MM/PBSA uncertainty.","latest_verdict":"untested","label":"agent-generated hypothesis"},{"id":"H3","mechanism_class":"stability_folding","starting_rank":3,"statement":"R28H destabilises the PH domain fold. The residue lies in the beta strand (residues 25-32) and its arginine side chain makes intra-domain packing or salt-bridge contacts that the histidine cannot keep, which lowers folding stability and reduces the amount of soluble, folded protein.","supports":["E7","E10","E12","E18"],"would_refute":"Predicted ΔΔG for R28H from folding-stability tools (run on the AlphaFold DB model AF-Q06187-F1 and on 1B55 and 6TT2) is below about 1 kcal/mol, and residue 28 is solvent-exposed with no buried intra-domain partner in the crystal structures or in the AlphaFold model, so the side chain makes no packing contact to remove.","latest_verdict":"untested","label":"agent-generated hypothesis"}],"results":[{"test_id":"T1","test_kind":"ligand_contact","summary":"Residue 28 lies within 4.5 Å of an organic ligand in 32 of 39 ligand-bound experimental structures, with the closest contact at 2.58 Å to 4PT in PDB 2Z0P (chain A and C). Negative-control ligands (3IS, 72V, A1JS1, IS7, MG, NYQ, Q1B, ZN) never contacted the residue, and contacting ligands had median neighbour counts of 9.5–13 residues, so the contacts are not from large neighbour lists. In the four structures carrying the R28C mutation (6TT2, 6TSE, 1BTK, 6YYF), no ligand instance contacted residue 28.","headline":"Residue 28 is within 4.5 Å of an organic ligand in 32 of 39 ligand-bound structures (4IP, 4PT, A1B6F, A1B6G, A1B6H, A1B6I); closest 2.58 Å to 4PT ((2R)-3-{[(S)-{[(2S,3R,5S,6S)-2,6-DIHYDROXY-3,4,5-TRIS(PHOSPHONOOXY)CY…) in PDB 2Z0P.","verdict":"contact_with_organic_ligand","job_id":null}]}
